content:
I'm sure many of you are curious about the new autoformatter but what many of you might not know is that the new autoformatter is already available to try at the draft PR lean4#15218! So if you want to try it out (without mathlib), you can use the lean-toolchain leanprover/lean4-pr-releases:pr-release-15218. But I also decided to format all of mathlib with it and put it as a branch on my mathlib fork for anyone to view here!

Some notes:

  • The branch only builds on my machine because it uses a local toolchain
  • I only touched Mathlib, not Archive etc.
  • I did not add any formatters for mathlib specific syntax! That means that mathlib syntax was not touched by the formatter and might look weird in the context of everything around it being formatted (this includes e.g. lemma commands!)
  • The formatter worked very well on almost all files; except for 12. I'm not entirely sure why; my guess is that this might be due to some mathlib-specific syntax breaking things
  • Almost all files built successfully after formatting; except for two: Mathlib.Data.Finset.Max and Mathlib.Data.Fintype.EquivFin. This is because of a parsing special case related to the cases tactic
  • The resulting code produced a ton of warnings, here is the full list. Most of them are either too long lines, too long files, style linters, or formatter errors
This is great! Can the autoformatter be made aware of the 100 character line length limit that we use in mathlib?
It is technically aware; it gets mostly wrong in the presence of comments

Here's a random example:

    calc
      (∑ k ∈ Ico 1 n.succ, (k : ℚ) ^ p.succ) -- replace sum over `Ico` with sum over `range` and simplify
      _ = ∑ k ∈ range n.succ, (k : ℚ) ^ p.succ := by simp [sum_Ico_eq_sub _ hle]

where the second line is too long
Was the comment on a separate line originally? Or is it that the autoformatter added brackets that pushed it over the limit?

Hmm this is the original:

  calc
    (-- replace sum over `Ico` with sum over `range` and simplify
        ∑ k ∈ Ico 1 n.succ, (k : ℚ) ^ p.succ)
    _ = ∑ k ∈ range n.succ, (k : ℚ) ^ p.succ := by simp [sum_Ico_eq_sub _ hle]
I don't think the autoformatter adds or removes brackets
At the end of the PR description, it says that the autoformatter adds brackets in a few rare cases.

Here's another egregious example:

instance : IsUniformGroup (α →ᵤ G) :=
  ⟨(UniformFun.postcomp_uniformContinuous uniformContinuous_div).comp -- Since `(/) : G × G → G` is uniformly continuous,
                                                                      -- `UniformFun.postcomp_uniformContinuous` tells us that
                                                                      -- `((/) ∘ —) : (α →ᵤ G × G) → (α →ᵤ G)` is uniformly continuous too. By precomposing with
                                                                      -- `UniformFun.uniformEquivProdArrow`, this gives that
                                                                      -- `(/) : (α →ᵤ G) × (α →ᵤ G) → (α →ᵤ G)` is also uniformly continuous
    UniformFun.uniformEquivProdArrow.symm.uniformContinuous⟩

where we originally had

/-- Let `𝔖 : Set (Set α)`. If `G` is a uniform group, then `α →ᵤ[𝔖] G` is a uniform group as
well. -/
@[to_additive /-- Let `𝔖 : Set (Set α)`. If `G` is a uniform additive group,
then `α →ᵤ[𝔖] G` is a uniform additive group as well. -/]
instance : IsUniformGroup (α →ᵤ[𝔖] G) :=
  ⟨(-- Since `(/) : G × G → G` is uniformly continuous,
    -- `UniformOnFun.postcomp_uniformContinuous` tells us that
    -- `((/) ∘ —) : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] G × G) → (α →ᵤ[𝔖] G)` is uniformly continuous too. By precomposing with
    -- `UniformOnFun.uniformEquivProdArrow`, this gives that
    -- `(/) : (α →ᵤ[𝔖] G) × (α →ᵤ[𝔖] G) → (α →ᵤ[𝔖] G)` is also uniformly continuous
    UniformOnFun.postcomp_uniformContinuous uniformContinuous_div).comp
    UniformOnFun.uniformEquivProdArrow.symm.uniformContinuous⟩

It seems like the formatter is in particular struggling with comments after brackets

We'll provide a way to review the diff from formatting Mathlib and core when I'm back from PTO.

As for comment formatting: comment formatting is very tricky in general, and we accept that there will always be cases where comments are not placed exactly where you want them to be placed. You should always be able to move comments to the right position after formatting in the few cases where you don't like the placement in the formatted document.

In this case, the problem is that line comments at the end of the line get associated with the preceding token, whereas the intent here was that the comment should be associated with the code on the line after it. Since a line break after a bracket is not legal in our set of formatting constraints, it ends up at the end of the line instead.

(There are some subtle idempotency-related issues with moving comments to the front of the line if they exceed the column width, so we don't do that anymore)

I'm in a place with very bad internet connectivity at the moment, so I can't respond to inquiries about the formatter until I get back from vacation. I also think it is better to wait with these discussions (ideally in the form of feedback to me directly) until we provide a nice way to view the full diff.
